an average fuel economy standard of 18.7 mpg. The standard proposed would apply to nonpassenger automobiles of no more than 6,000 GVWR manufactured in MY 1979. All nonpassenger atuomobiles less than 6000 pounds GVWR were treated as a single class. For purposes of the proposed rule, it was assumed that emissions standards applicable to nonpassenger automobiles in MY 1979 would not impose difficulties in improving fuel economy. In short, the standard was intended to be set close to the stated product plans of nonpassenger automobile manufacturers. The preamble to the proposed standard, which should be consulted for a detailed explanation of the basis of the agency action, discussed various ways in which the standard could be met, in order to demonstrate that the proposed standard was technologically feasible and economically practicable. Comments on the proposed fuel economy standard were to be filed by January 10, 1976.
Also on November 26, 1976, a draft environmental impact statement relating the proposed nonpassenger automobile fuel economy standard was filed with the Council on Environmental Quality. Comments on the draft environmental impact statement were to be filed by January 17, 1977.
